## Natural history notes

A large grasshopper characterized by its long body, strong hind legs, brown to greenish-brown coloration, and long wings that allow strong, sustained flight. In Florida, it is common in gardens, fields, roadsides, citrus groves, agricultural areas, pine flatwoods, parks, and other open or semi-open habitats with abundant vegetation. It feeds on leaves of many herbaceous plants, shrubs, and trees, sometimes becoming noticeable as a garden or crop pest, and usually escapes disturbance by powerful jumps followed by short flights.
